subject: science
domain: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

items.prompt:
The change in an object's motion depends on the net force and the object's:
A) Color
B) Mass
C) Name
D) Age

steps: Newton's Second Law relates the change in motion to net force and mass.

items.prompt:
The net force is:
A) Only the largest force
B) The sum of all forces on an object
C) Always zero
D) The object's weight only
items.answer: B) The sum of all forces on an object

steps: Net force is the sum of all forces acting on an object.

items.prompt:
If the net force on an object is zero, its motion:
A) Increases
B) Does not change
C) Reverses
D) Doubles

steps: Balanced forces mean no change in motion.

items.prompt:
You push two carts with the same force. The lighter cart will:
A) Speed up less
B) Speed up more
C) Not move
D) Move backward

steps: Less mass means more acceleration for the same force.

items.prompt:
A box has 12 N pushing right and 5 N pushing left. The net force is:
A) 17 N right
B) 7 N right
C) 7 N left
D) 0 N

steps: 12 N - 5 N = 7 N to the right.

items.prompt:
Keeping mass the same, increasing the net force on an object will:
A) Decrease its acceleration
B) Increase its acceleration
C) Stop it
D) Not matter

Why is it harder to accelerate a loaded truck than an empty one with the same force?
A) The loaded truck has more mass, so it accelerates less
B) Mass does not matter
C) The empty truck has more mass
D) Force changes with color
items.answer: A) The loaded truck has more mass, so it accelerates less

steps: Greater mass resists changes in motion.

items.prompt:
A cart moves at a constant speed in a straight line. The forces on it must be:
A) Unbalanced
B) Balanced (net force zero)
C) Only one force
D) Increasing

steps: Constant straight-line motion means the net force is zero.
